name: Solid Tumor Associated with an Acquired Peripheral Neuropathy

criteria.description: Presence of acquired peripheral neuropathy with sensory and/or motor deficits
Confirmed diagnosis of a solid tumor malignancy by histopathology or imaging
Detection of paraneoplastic antibodies associated with neuropathy (e.g., anti-Hu, anti-CV2/CRMP5)
Exclusion of other common causes of peripheral neuropathy such as diabetes, toxins, or infections
Electrophysiological studies consistent with axonal or demyelinating peripheral neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of acquired peripheral neuropathy with confirmed solid tumor malignancy and exclusion of other neuropathy causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Paraneoplastic antibodies support diagnosis but are not always present.

pathognomonic.notes: Characterized by asymmetric sensory loss and proprioceptive deficits

searchTerms: rapid muscle weakness in arms and legs
pins and needles in distal extremities
reduced or missing muscle stretch reflexes

common.symptomName: Gait ataxia due to sensory loss
searchTerms: balance problems due to nerve damage
muscle wasting in hands or feet
loss of muscle bulk in fingers or toes

occasional.symptomName: Neuropathic pain with burning or shooting quality
searchTerms: tingling burning pain in arms or legs
mild problems with balance and coordination
impaired coordination due to sensory loss

rare.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness leading to dyspnea
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness

rare.symptomName: Bladder dysfunction due to autonomic neuropathy
Cutaneous vasculitis associated with paraneoplastic syndrome

laboratory: Presence of paraneoplastic antibodies (e.g., anti-Hu, anti-CV2/CRMP5)
Elevated inflammatory markers in some cases
Normal or mildly elevated tumor markers depending on tumor type
imaging: MRI of peripheral nerves may show nerve enlargement or enhancement
CT or PET scan to identify underlying solid tumor
Electromyography and nerve conduction studies showing axonal or demyelinating neuropathy
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; diagnosis is clinical and paraneoplastic antibody-based

distinguishingFeatures: No associated tumor or paraneoplastic antibodies
No direct association with solid tumors

redFlags: New onset peripheral neuropathy in patient with known or suspected malignancy
Presence of paraneoplastic antibodies in serum or CSF
references: Darnell RB, Posner JB. Paraneoplastic Syndromes Affecting the Nervous System. Semin Oncol. 2006;33(3):270-298.
Graus F, Delattre JY, Antoine JC, et al. Recommended diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurological syndromes. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 2004;75(8):1135-1140.
Vialatte de Pémille C, et al. Paraneoplastic neuropathies: clinical and electrophysiological features. Rev Neurol (Paris). 2019;175(3):163-172.
